Subject: Dedicated capacity preflight: token mix, concurrency & burst profile for DeltaHealth pilot

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To size the dedicated GPU pool for the pilot and draft an SLA, we need a short traffic + prompt questionnaire filled out. If you can return the CSV and the answers below it will let us produce a preliminary sizing and cost estimate within 48 hours.

Quick asks (can paste answers in reply or send files):
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and typical response length (tokens). If you have distributions, include P50/P90.
- Peak concurrent sessions expected during 1-hour windows (and any predictable daily peaks).
- Burst tolerance: how long can performance degrade before it impacts customers? (e.g., 1 min, 5 mins)
- Ratio of chat-style sessions to short-completion calls (percent).
- Session lifetime: are you pinning sessions (long KV cache) or stateless per-request? Typical session duration in minutes.
- Estimated percent of requests that require >1024 context (if any).

Attachments I can accept: raw token logs, sampled request CSV (timestamp,user_id,model,prompt_tokens,resp_tokens,latency_ms).

I'll loop Ben for the initial capacity sketch once we have the sample.

Thanks —

Camila Reyes

From: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@deltahealth.ai>

Cc: ops@deltahealth.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Sep 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity preflight: token mix, concurrency & burst profile for DeltaHealth pilot

Camila —

Thanks, appreciate the clear list. Attaching a sampled export and a short spreadsheet that summarizes token distributions. Answers inline below and the CSV is attached (delta_traffic_sample_q3.csv).

- Typical prompt length: P50=85 tokens, P90=320 tokens.
- Typical response length: P50=160 tokens, P90=680 tokens.
- Peak concurrency: currently we expect 350 concurrent sessions sustained for 15–20 minutes during our morning surge (09:00–09:30 PT) and a smaller evening surge ~120 concurrent.
- Burst tolerance: we need <2x degradation in latency for up to 3 minutes; after that SLA should failover to fallback model.
- Chat vs short completions: ~70% chat-style, 30% short completions (webhooks).
- Session lifetime: sessions are stateful; median session duration 18 minutes, but top 5% last >2 hours (they keep long KV caches).
- >1024 context: ~12% of requests exceed 1024 tokens; 3% exceed 2048.

We also included a sample of high-concurrency hour (09:00 PT) as delta_traffic_sample_q3.csv and a short prompt-mix summary (delta_prompt_mix_summary.xlsx). Let me know if you need anything else.

—Ethan

FYI forwarding DeltaHealth's sample and their answers. Key points: 350 concurrent during morning surge, long session tails (top 5% >2h), 12% >1024 context. They require <2x latency degradation for 3 minutes before failover.

Ben — can you sketch an initial dedicated pool that covers their P90 token sizes and session behavior? Specifically:
- GPU mix recommendation (A100xlarge vs H100/8q etc) and rough # of GPUs to meet 350 concurrent at P90 with room for 25% burst headroom.
- Cache strategy: recommend session pinning approach (affinity / KV partitioning) to support long sessions while keeping occupancy low.
- Failover plan: automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant after 3 minutes of overload and how that affects user experience.

Marissa — can you draft a one-page SLA note with the degradation window and failover behavior we propose? I attached our SLA_proposal_v1.pdf stub as starting template.

Thanks —
Camila

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 14 Sep 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity preflight: token mix, concurrency & burst profile for DeltaHealth pilot

Thanks for the forward — quick sizing sketch below (high-level, for internal kickoff).

Executive summary:
- Recommended initial pool: 8 x H100-80GB (quantized runtime) with adaptive batching and session affinity. This gives headroom for 350 concurrent chat sessions at P90 token sizes with 25% spare capacity.
- For the long-session tail: reserve a small pool of 2 GPUs for pinned sessions (LongKV) with strict eviction for idle >30m — use affinity hashing by customer shard to limit cross-tenant KV blowup.
- Fallback plan: after 3 minutes of sustained overload we shift 20% of requests to a lower-cost Llama3-13B-8q variant with slightly trimmed context (compressive summarization) — expect 10–15% quality delta. This satisfies their <2x latency tolerance window.
- Estimated monthly committed cost (infra only): (ballpark) $69k/month — will refine after we run a micro-sim using their CSV.

Next steps:
1) I'll run a simulated micro-benchmark using delta_traffic_sample_q3.csv (will share results + precise GPU-hours).
2) Marissa drafts SLA note and we align on failover messaging to their ops team (Ethan).
3) Confirm whether DeltaHealth wants pinned sessions to be single-tenant only or tenantized pinned pools.

I'll kick off the micro-sim tonight and update HubSpot with the numbers.
